articles.text: LÍN LǍOSHĪ: Zài niàn shénme ne?
TEACHER LÍN: What are you reading?
MĚIGUÓ XUÉSHENG: Ō, Lín Lǎoshī, nín hǎo! Wǒ zài kàn Lǔ Xùn Xiānshengde xiǎoshuō.
AMERICAN STUDENT: Oh, Miss Lín (Teacher Lín), how are you! I'm reading some fiction by Mr. Lǔ Xùn.
LÍN LǍOSHĪ: Shi něipiān na?
TEACHER LÍN: What piece?
MĚIGUÓ XUÉSHENG: "Yào." Wǒ hěn xǐhuan Lǔ Xùn Xiānshengde xiǎoshuō.
AMERICAN STUDENT: "Medicine." I like Lǔ Xùn's fiction very much.
LÍN LǍOSHĪ: Wǒ xiǎng, zài Měiguóde shíhou, Zhōngguó lìshǐ, Zhōngguó wénxué, nǐ dàgài niànde bù shǎo.
TEACHER LÍN: I guess you've probably read quite a lot of Chinese history and literature in America.

MĚIGUÓ XUÉSHENG: Xué Zhōngwén, dāngrán shǒuxiān xué yìdiǎnr lìshǐ hé wénxué, dǒng yìdiǎnr Zhōngguó wénhuà, yàoburán xué Zhōngwén yídìng yǒu hěn dàde kùnnan. Zhōngguó liúxuéshēng yě shi zhèiyang zuò ma?

AMERICAN STUDENT: To study the Chinese language, you have to first study a little history and literature, and understand a little Chinese culture, otherwise you're sure to have a hard time studying the language. Do Chinese who go abroad to study do the same thing?
LÍN LǍOSHĪ: Wǒmende xuéxí tiáojiàn hái shi bú cuòde, kěshi liúxuéshēng chū guó yǐqián děi duì nèige guójiāde wénhuà zuò bìyàode liǎojiě. Zài zhèifāngmiàn, wǒmen zuòde hái hěn bú gòu.

TEACHER LÍN: Our conditions for study are fairly good, but before a student goes abroad, he ought to acquire the requisite understanding of the country he is going to. In this area, we have as yet done far from enough.
MĚIGUÓ XUÉSHENG: Wǒ tīngshuō Zhōngguó liúxuéshēngde niánlíng dōu bú tài xiǎo le, duō shi Wénhuà Dà Gémìng yǐqián bìyède.
AMERICAN STUDENT: I understand that the Chinese students going abroad aren't very young; most of them graduated from college before the Cultural Revolution.
LÍN LǍOSHĪ: Shì. Wénhuà Dà Gémìng yǐqiánde dàxué bìyèshēng pǔbiànde zhìliàng bǐjiào gāo, hé Wéngé yǐhòude dàxuéshēng chābié bù xiǎo.
TEACHER LÍN: Yes. In general the quality of college graduates from before the Cultural Revolution is higher. They're quite different from the post-Cultural Revolution college students.
MĚIGUÓ XUÉSHENG: Nàme shùliàng ne?
AMERICAN STUDENT: How about in terms of numbers?
LÍN LǍOSHĪ: Shùliàng yě bù shǎo.
TEACHER LÍN: Their numbers are quite large, too.
MĚIGUÓ XUÉSHENG: Nàme zhèixiē bìyèshēng shì bu shì dōu dānrèn bǐjiào zhòngyàode gōngzuò ne?
AMERICAN STUDENT: So do these graduates all take on rather important jobs?

LÍN LǍOSHĪ: Bù dōu yíyàng. Mùqián, Wénhuà Dà Gémìng yǐqiánde dàxué bìyèshēng yǒu hěn duō dānrèn bǐjiào zhòngyàode gōngzuò. Bǐfang shuō wǒmen Xuéyuàn ba, gōngzuòde bǐjiào hǎode duōbànr shi nèige shíhourde dàxuéshēng. Dāngrán, hái yǒu gèng lǎode.

TEACHER LÍN: They're not all the same. At present, there are many pre-Cultural Revolution college graduates who have taken on rather important jobs. For example, in our Institute, those who do their work comparatively well are mostly college students from that time. Of course there are older ones as well.
MĚIGUÓ XUÉSHENG: Wǒ hěn xǐhuan wǒmende lǎoshī, yě hěn xǐhuan Yǔyán Xuéyuàn, wǒ zhǐ shi xīwang yǒu bǐjiào duōde jīhui gēn Zhōngguó xuésheng, lǎoshī duō tǎotán.
AMERICAN STUDENT: I like our teachers very much, and the Institute, too. I just wish we would have more opportunities to talk with the Chinese students and teachers.
LÍN LǍOSHĪ: Hǎo, hǎo, yǒu shíjiān wǒmen duō tántan. Nǐ kàn shū ba. Yìhuǐr jiàn.
TEACHER LÍN: All right, we'll talk more when we get the time. You go on reading. See you in a while.
MĚIGUÓ XUÉSHENG: Lín Lǎoshī yìhuǐr jiàn.
AMERICAN STUDENT: See you in a while, Miss Lín.
